subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Screw: A Spiral Ramp
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Screw: A Spiral Ramp usable.

hook.text: A screw is just an inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder. Twist it and it climbs.

buildup.text: Each turn advances the screw by one pitch — the distance between threads. Tight threads mean more force.

discovery.text: Archimedes used this idea to lift water. His screw pump moved river water uphill to irrigate fields.

twist.text: A car jack uses a screw. One hand turning a handle can lift a two-ton vehicle off the ground.

climax.text: Screws hold buildings together, press olives into oil, and move 3D printer heads with precision.

punchline.text: Wrap a ramp around a rod and you get one of history's best ideas.

quiz.question: What does tighter thread spacing on a screw accomplish?
options: It allows the screw to spin faster with less effort
It increases force output but requires more turns to advance
It reduces friction so the screw slides in more smoothly
